summary: 2026-09-17: Got NT8 BacktestRunner automation fully working end-to-end (task t-b2d143). Root-caused 3 real bugs blocking it: (1) AddOns only instantiate at NT8 startup, not on recompile - close+reopen NT8 needed after any AddOn change. (2) NT8's global Time Zone (Tools>Options>General) was set to Kuala Lumpur/UTC+8 instead of Central Time - since our imported ES data + Orb.cs's hardcoded range times (830/845/1030) are all Central, this silently shifted every bar's clock so the 8:30-8:45 range window never matched a real bar -> 0 trades always. Fixed: user set it to 'Central Time (US & Canada)'. (3) Custom instrument ES_1M_2024 (and presumably other ES_1M_20xx years) was created with wrong contract specs: TickSize=0.01, PointValue=1 (stock-like defaults) instead of real ES 0.25/50 - user fixed TickSize and PointValue via Tools>Instruments (PointValue field was initially locked/greyed at 1 but became editable and user changed it to 50 successfully). Also discovered: NT8 AddOns need a forced recompile (open NinjaScript Editor, open BacktestRunner.cs, press F5) to actually start watching jobs/ each NT8 session - a plain close/reopen was NOT enough on the 2nd/3rd restart (unclear why it worked once on the very first restart last session but not since - suspect that first time coincided with the original post-edit compile). After the forced F5 recompile with NinjaScript Output window open, jobs test2.job and test3.job (both Orb/ES_1M_2024/Jan-2024) WERE picked up and processed automatically end-to-end with zero clicks (this is the actual proof the no-click pipeline works) - NinjaScript Output showed correct range/breakout prints every trading day (e.g. 'Orb 2024-01-02: range 4818.75-4820.50, breakout 4820.75/4818.50, session-start bar Time[0]=08:46'), confirming the timezone fix worked. BUT result was TotalTrades=0, PercentProfitable=0, yet NetProfit=50 (contradiction) for both. Read FormatPerformance() in BacktestRunner.cs (uses perf.AllTrades.Count for TotalTrades, perf.AllTrades.TradesPerformance.NetProfit for NetProfit) - suspect NetProfit reflects an unrealized/open position at the exact end of the requested date range (to=2024-02-01 may cut off mid-day) that never got closed, so it never became a completed Trade in AllTrades but still shows floating PnL. Also saw exactly one 'Internal Order Handling Rules... Enter() ignored' warning at the very first entry attempt (2024-01-02 08:46) only, never repeated on later days - not yet explained. To test the mid-cutoff theory, dropped test4.job (same strategy/instrument, but from=2024-01-01 to=2024-06-01, a full 5 months) - this was still processing (background poll task bovdpz1ry, not yet returned a result) when this session hit its context limit. User is understandably frustrated with the amount of manual GUI clicking needed and asked if this can be more automated - answered honestly: the job-drop-to-result pipeline itself is now proven zero-click; the friction so far has been one-time NT8 platform setup (timezone, instrument specs, forced recompile) with no documented headless alternative.
next_steps: 1. Check ninjascript/results/test4.result.txt (5-month Jan-Jun 2024 Orb/ES_1M_2024 run) - if TotalTrades>0 now, the mid-window-cutoff theory is confirmed and results are trustworthy; also delete/ignore the stray test1-4.job files in ninjascript/jobs/done/ once satisfied. 2. If test4 STILL shows 0 trades despite a full 5-month window, the bug is real (not just a cutoff artifact) - next debugging step: add temporary Print() lines inside ArmEntries()/OnOrderUpdate() in Orb.cs to log every EnterLongStopMarket/EnterShortStopMarket call and every fill, since NT8 Output only currently prints on range-set, not on actual order submission/fill - this needs one more forced-recompile (F5 in NinjaScript Editor with Output window open, same ritual as this session) after editing. 3. Still unexplained: why the 'Internal Order Handling Rules ignored' warning printed exactly once (first entry of the whole test) and never again on subsequent days - worth understanding before trusting trade counts, may indicate every day's short-side (or long-side) entry is silently getting rejected the same way but NT8 suppresses the repeated identical message text. 4. Once Orb.cs produces real, sane trade counts end-to-end via the automation, do the actual test.registry/prop_sim comparison this whole task was originally for. 5. Note for future sessions: AddOn changes need a full NT8 close+reopen AND a forced F5 recompile in NinjaScript Editor (with NinjaScript Output open) each session before jobs/ get picked up - a plain reopen was not reliably enough this session.
questions: Why did the very first NT8 restart last session pick up a job automatically without a forced F5 recompile, but the 2nd and 3rd restarts this session did not? If we understand this we could maybe avoid the manual recompile step in future.
